gap: No result ChatGPT got states that base M1 and M2 MacBook Airs and 13-inch MacBook Pros, and the M3 Air with its lid open, can drive only one external display and have no native MST; TESmart says this, so two of the three cards ChatGPT showed (the CKL 922HUA-3 and the $359 TESmart HKS202-M24 HDMI 2.1 Dual 4K144Hz Gaming Dock) can give those Macs only one screen, and TESmart's stated fix is a DisplayLink dock or KVM.
standout_why: I compared against DockGearHQ 'Best KVM Switches with HDMI (2026)', DeskDNA 'Best KVM Switch for 2 Computers', TheTechSearch 'Best KVM Switches for Two Computers in 2026', OfficeKitHQ 'Best KVM Switch with HDMI', and GearExplained 'best KVM switches'. None of them mentions the single-external-display limit of Apple silicon. GearExplained comes closest: for the TESmart CKS202-P23 it says only that 'Macs need two cables and may be limited on a single path.' DockGearHQ covers other compatibility points, which are therefore not new: the HDK202-P23-V2 needs two separate video connections per host, the UGREEN CM731's USB-C input needs DP Alt Mode, emulated keyboard ports refuse Bluetooth and some gaming keyboards, and the UGREEN 55397 needs short HDMI 2.1 cables. DeskDNA and TheTechSearch only say every pick is 'plug-and-play on macOS'. OfficeKitHQ says 'Apple silicon external display limits' are not stated. thisUSB could not be read because of a certificate error.
decides: If either computer is a base M1 or M2 MacBook Air or 13-inch MacBook Pro, or an M3 Air used with the lid open, a dual-monitor HDMI KVM like the TESmart HKS202-M24 or the CKL 922HUA-3 will not extend that Mac across two screens. That shopper should buy a 2-PC, 1-monitor HDMI KVM such as the UGREEN CM664/15707, or a DisplayLink-based KVM. Shoppers with two PCs, or a Mac on a Pro or Max chip, are unaffected, and the dual-monitor picks stand for them. The HKS202-M24 also needs two HDMI outputs per computer, because its inputs are HDMI and HDMI. Separately, TESmart's own store showed the US-plug HKS202-M24 out of stock today.

findings.product: general (Apple silicon MacBooks on any KVM)
findings.label: MacBooks limited to one external display
findings.value: M1 and M2 MacBook Pro 13-inch and MacBook Air, the M3 Air (lid open) and the M3 Pro 14-inch (lid open) 'support only one external display'
findings.source_title: MacBook M1/M2 Users, Take Note: Achieving Triple 4K Display Output & Performance Insights (TESmart, dated 2025-03-18)
findings.note: This is TESmart's own blog, from a KVM maker. It also says 'M1 and M2 MacBooks inherently lack support for multiple external displays due to hardware limitations.' Apple's own per-model page was not opened (see unsourced). The listing for the 'M3 Pro 14-inch (lid open)' is TESmart's wording and conflicts with how M3 Pro machines are usually specced, so do not repeat that part of the claim.

findings.product: general (Apple silicon MacBooks on any KVM)
findings.label: No native MST on these Macs
findings.value: These MacBooks 'do not natively support Multi-Stream Transport (MST)' despite having several Thunderbolt ports
findings.source_title: MacBook M1/M2 Users, Take Note: Achieving Triple 4K Display Output & Performance Insights (TESmart)
findings.note: Without MST, one USB-C cable into a dual-monitor KVM cannot extend to two screens from these Macs.

findings.product: general (Apple silicon MacBooks on any KVM)

findings.note: The author's own test used a TESmart HDC203-PM24 with a DisplayLink DL-6950 chip and reports three displays showing in System Report. That is one test, not a spec.
